clue.text: Innocent Charles starts to take Ecstasy

parts.note: Chas is the usual short form of the name Charles

indicators.note: starts points to the opening letter of each of the next two words

explanation.surface: Respectable Charles begins experimenting with party drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charles' looks like the subject of the sentence, but only his short name is used; 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone pure and untouched by sexual experience.

clue.text: Advice on clues in anagram form

indicators.note: the clue says outright that the letters of on and clues are to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A solver is offered tips on how to tackle anagram clues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in anagram form' rearranges ON and CLUES together.
explanation.definitionFit: Counsel is a formal word for guidance given to someone.

clue.text: One taken in at start of month

definitions.text: One taken in at start of month

parts.words: One taken in at start of month
parts.note: someone deceived by a prank on the first day of the fourth month of the year

explanation.surface: Someone admitted at the beginning of a calendar month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken in' looks like admitted or housed, but means fooled; the month start is the first of April.
explanation.definitionFit: The victim of a prank played on 1 April is given this name.

clue.text: He critically examines an old coin

definitions.meaning: someone who checks or trials things
a sixpence of Tudor times, later slang for the sixpenny piece

explanation.surface: An expert scrutinises an antique coin.
explanation.walkthrough: A tester was an old English coin, originally a shilling of Henry VIII, later slang for sixpence.
explanation.definitionFit: One who checks things tests them, and the old silver coin happens to share the spelling.

clue.text: Power worker who fought with the Resistance

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for power
an artisan is a skilled manual worker

explanation.surface: An electricity worker who served in the wartime underground movement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Power worker' suggests someone at a power station, but splits into P and a craftsman.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the armed underground in occupied wartime Europe were called by this name.

clue.text: Signal a smile conceals, unfortunately

indicators.note: the phrase Signal a smile keeps the run of letters tucked within it

explanation.surface: A smile can hide bad news, regrettably.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation expresses regret, much as the adverb does at the start of a sentence.

clue.text: William's account as a whistle blower

parts.note: William Tell, the Swiss folk hero, gives his surname
a tale is an account or story

explanation.surface: A man named William tells his story as an informer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as a' is a link; William Tell is the legendary Swiss archer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who reports on others' wrongdoing is a sneak or informer.

clue.text: Assets to face in times of adversity

definitions.text: Assets to face in times of adversity

parts.words: Assets to face in times of adversity
parts.note: features of the face that are useful when hard times come, meaning a stoic, unemotional manner

explanation.surface: Resources needed to confront difficult periods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'face' reads as a verb (confront) but is the noun: the assets sit on the face. The British ideal of not showing emotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping the mouth firm and unmoved is the idiom for stoical endurance in trouble.

clue.text: Students around district barely enjoy themselves

indicators.note: around shows the students' letters being placed either side of district's abbreviation

parts.note: NUS is the National Union of Students

explanation.surface: Students in a local area have fun wearing next to nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barely' means without clothes, not hardly.
explanation.definitionFit: Naturists take their pleasure unclothed, so they enjoy themselves bare.

clue.text: Peacekeepers stay in time of strife

parts.note: UN peacekeeping forces are United Nations troops
to rest is to stay or remain

explanation.surface: Peacekeeping troops remain during a period of conflict.
explanation.definitionFit: Unrest is disturbance or turmoil, a period of conflict in society.

clue.text: Nick a pheasant, say — you may end up thus

parts.note: nick is British slang for prison
a pheasant is an example of a bird

explanation.surface: Steal a game bird and you might wind up a prisoner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nick' reads as steal, but here is the noun, British slang for prison.
explanation.definitionFit: A poacher who is caught ends up a convict, a habitual prisoner.

clue.text: Month birds generally make musical notes

parts.note: Oct is the abbreviation for October
Aves is the scientific class name covering all birds

explanation.surface: In a certain month, birds sing tunes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make' is a link; Aves is the Latin class of birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Notes eight steps apart on the scale share a letter name; such intervals and their top notes are so called.

clue.text: Sixpence left over ensured it for Mr Micawber

definitions.text: Sixpence left over ensured it for Mr Micawber

parts.words: Sixpence left over ensured it for Mr Micawber
parts.note: Dickens's Micawber said income of twenty pounds against spending of nineteen pounds nineteen and six meant happiness

explanation.surface: A Dickens character's remark about a small surplus.
explanation.walkthrough: In David Copperfield, Mr Micawber says spending sixpence less than you earn brings happiness, and sixpence more brings misery.
explanation.definitionFit: Having income just above spending is the state of being able to pay one's debts.

clue.text: Bodies of teachers found in the Midlands

definitions.meaning: short name of a county in the English Midlands

explanation.surface: Teaching personnel are located in central England.
explanation.walkthrough: Staffordshire, a county in central England, is abbreviated this way.
explanation.definitionFit: A school's employees form its teaching personnel; the county name Staffordshire shortens to the same letters.

clue.text: A French costume popular with 8

parts.note: un is French for a
a dress is a costume or outfit

explanation.surface: A French outfit loved by naturists.
explanation.walkthrough: 8 is NUDISTS; undress as a noun means a state of having little or no clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Naturists favour being without clothes, the state of being unclothed.

clue.text: Spoils device when put in reverse

indicators.note: put in reverse means the word for device is read backwards

parts.note: a tool is a device or instrument

explanation.surface: A gadget is ruined by being driven backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spoils' looks like a verb but is the noun, plunder; 'when' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Plunder taken in war or crime is booty.

clue.text: Signs of depression don't bother gardeners

definitions.meaning: a weather depression brings grey skies heralding wet weather
they save gardeners the trouble of watering

explanation.surface: Indicators of low mood are no concern to those who garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'depression' means low pressure in weather, not low spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Dark clouds accompany a low-pressure system, and they bring water that gardens welcome.

clue.text: See 7
It could be simple amusement

definitions.meaning: in finance, simple and compound kinds of return on money exist

explanation.surface: Something could be just plain fun.
explanation.definitionFit: Simple interest is a finance term; interest also means attention or entertainment value.

clue.text: Lover's tune adapted for soldiers

indicators.note: adapted signals that the letters of the phrase are rearranged into a new form

parts.note: the possessive s is read as a letter here, giving lovers

explanation.surface: A romantic's song is rearranged for troops.
explanation.definitionFit: Troops who enlist of their own free will rather than being conscripted.

clue.text: He scored every season

parts.note: a composer who wrote music for each of the four seasons

explanation.surface: A sportsman who got goals in every season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scored' suggests a footballer but means composed music; The Four Seasons is a set of violin concertos.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian Baroque composer wrote The Four Seasons concertos.

clue.text: Box largely surplus to requirements

indicators.note: largely means most of the word is used, with its last letter dropped

parts.note: spare means extra, surplus to what is needed

explanation.surface: A carton that is mostly unneeded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Box' is a verb, to fight with fists, not a container.
explanation.definitionFit: To spar is to box, especially in practice.

clue.text: Dodgy schemes, we hear? More than likely!

annotationWithheld.why: Dodgy schemes, we hear? More than likely! (7): 'Dodgy schemes' gives RACKETS, but no reading of 'we hear? More than likely!' as wordplay producing those letters could be found or confirmed
annotationWithheld.clue: Dodgy schemes, we hear? More than likely!

clue.text: For example, points go up for starchy food

indicators.note: in a down clue, go up means the run is read from bottom to top

parts.note: eg is the abbreviation of exempli gratia, for example
dots are points

explanation.surface: Points on a menu rise for a heavy, filling dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go up' turns the whole of EG plus DOTS backwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavy, filling food like suet pudding is called stodge.

clue.text: Nameless wild flower

indicators.note: Nameless says to remove N, the abbreviation for name

parts.note: violent means wild or uncontrolled

explanation.surface: An anonymous wild flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild flower' reads as one phrase; 'wild' is the wordplay, 'flower' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The violet is a small purple flowering plant.

clue.text: Australia has one that's under threat globally

parts.note: Oz is a nickname for Australia

explanation.surface: Australia has something endangered worldwide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' is a link; 'globally' points to the planet's protective layer.
explanation.definitionFit: The atmospheric layer protecting Earth from ultraviolet rays has been depleted, famously over the southern hemisphere.

clue.text: Coteries, surprisingly, often are

indicators.note: surprisingly signals the letters of Coteries come out in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: Exclusive cliques tend to be obscure.
explanation.definitionFit: Small exclusive groups tend to be obscure and understood by only an inner circle.

clue.text: Bankrupt, yet holding a bit of stock

indicators.note: holding shows the word for yet enclosing another letter

parts.note: but and yet both mean however

indicators.note: a bit of picks the first letter of stock

explanation.surface: A broke trader still keeps a little stock.
explanation.definitionFit: Going bust means becoming insolvent, unable to pay one's debts.

clue.text: Relax: good advice when you're tight!

definitions.meaning: tight meaning stiff or tense, or literally too snug

explanation.surface: Advice to a tense or tipsy person to unwind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tight' can also mean drunk, a false trail.
explanation.definitionFit: To unwind is to become less stiff, the remedy for being tense or constricted.

clue.text: Guidance given by a duke on sin

parts.note: a vice is a sin or moral failing

explanation.surface: A nobleman offers counsel on wrongdoing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given by' and 'on' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Counsel or recommendations about what to do.

clue.text: Do you forget yourself in such a crisis?

definitions.text: Do you forget yourself in such a crisis?

parts.words: Do you forget yourself in such a crisis?
parts.note: a crisis in which a person loses track of who they really are

explanation.surface: A question about losing self-control in an emergency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forget yourself' usually means behave badly; here it means lose your sense of self, as in the phrase for a crisis about who one is.
explanation.definitionFit: A crisis of selfhood is when someone is unsure who they are.

clue.text: We have five suspects

definitions.meaning: humans have sight, hearing, smell, taste and touch
detects or perceives something is so

explanation.surface: A police team has five people under suspicion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspects' looks like a noun but is a verb, perceives.
explanation.definitionFit: Humans have five faculties of perception; to perceive vaguely is to suspect.
